Robot joints

Source: R/joints-links.R
robot_joint.Rd

A joint connects a parent link to a child link. The pose of the child link frame relative to the parent link frame is $${}^{parent}T_{child}(q) = T_{origin}\, M(q)\, T_{post},$$ where \(T_{origin}\) is the fixed joint frame (the URDF <origin>), \(M(q)\) is a rotation by \(q + offset\) about axis (revolute and continuous joints) or a translation by \((q + offset)\) along axis (prismatic joints), and \(T_{post}\) is an optional fixed transform applied after the motion. URDF joints use \(T_{post} = I\); Denavit-Hartenberg models use it to place the link frame at the DH frame. The axis is expressed in the joint frame and normalized.

Usage

robot_joint(
  name,
  type = c("revolute", "continuous", "prismatic", "fixed"),
  parent,
  child,
  origin = robot_pose(),
  axis = c(0, 0, 1),
  limits = NULL,
  velocity = NULL,
  acceleration = NULL,
  effort = NULL,
  offset = 0,
  post = NULL
)

Arguments

name

Joint name.

type

One of "revolute", "continuous", "prismatic", "fixed".

parent, child

Names of the parent and child links.

origin

Fixed robot_pose (SE(3)) of the joint frame in the parent link frame.

axis

Joint axis in the joint frame.

limits

Length-2 vector c(lower, upper) of position limits.

velocity, acceleration, effort

Optional nonnegative limits.

offset

Constant added to the joint variable before the motion.

post

Optional fixed robot_pose applied after the motion.

Value

A robot_joint object.

Details

Units are radians and meters. Revolute joints default to unbounded limits; continuous joints are always unbounded and reject finite limits. Velocity, acceleration and effort limits are optional (NULL means unspecified, not zero).

Examples

robot_joint("shoulder", "revolute", "base", "upper_arm",
            origin = transl(0, 0, 0.1), axis = c(0, 0, 1),
            limits = c(-pi, pi))
#> <robot_joint> shoulder (revolute): base -> upper_arm, axis (0, 0, 1) limits [-3.14159, 3.14159]
